# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Riley Ellison**
Member ID: W168862914
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield
Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-02 — Reference number POC-ACAA2D5BAD-67552**
**Member:** Riley Ellison | **Member ID:** W168862914
**Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
**Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), Colorado
**Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon) — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-02 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Anthem to reconsider that decision and to approve the procedure.

I believe the records already in Anthem's possession meet the criteria in the plan's own published guideline, the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon). Below I set out the plan's language and the matching records point by point.

## The plan's criteria and the records

**1. Documentation and plan of care.** The guideline states:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of components that was not reproduced in the excerpt available to me. If any specific component on that list was considered missing, I ask that Anthem identify it in writing so it can be supplied. The prior authorization packet submitted by Dr. Lindqvist included my symptom history, my conservative treatment history, my imaging, and my examination findings, and Dr. Lindqvist has documented that this procedure is needed.

**2. Conservative management — content.** The guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records show exactly that combination:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training, 8 weeks, from 2026-05-13 to 2026-07-08, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Complementary strategies (more than one):** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

**3. Conservative management — completion.** The guideline states:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

I completed the full course of physical therapy described above through discharge on 2026-07-08, alongside 8 months of NSAIDs and the injection, all within this episode of care.

**4. Response to conservative management.** The guideline states:

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My records describe 9 months of **progressive** pain in the neck, unrelieved by rest; NSAIDs with inadequate relief over 8 months; and an injection that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief before symptoms continued. My radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger, with weakness, persisted after conservative care was completed.

**5. Imaging.** The guideline states:

> "All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

My cervical spine MRI of 2026-06-07 shows a **C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression.** That imaging correlates directly with my clinical findings: radicular pain and numbness into the **right** thumb and index finger with weakness, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The study was performed at [name of imaging facility] and read by [name of interpreting radiologist]; a copy of the radiologist's report is enclosed.

**6. The indication itself.** The guideline states:

> "When imaging studies demonstrate nerve root compression due to herniated disc or spondylotic osteophyte correlating with the distribution of signs and symptoms, and ANY of the following criteria apply:"

The threshold condition in that sentence is met: my MRI demonstrates nerve root compression due to a herniated disc, and it correlates with the distribution of my symptoms. That sentence also ends in a colon, and the policy then lists further conditions of which **any one** may apply. From the excerpts available to me, my records meet the following:

> "Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, along with numbness into the right thumb and index finger and weakness — findings that correspond to the C6 nerve root compression seen on the 2026-06-07 MRI.

> "Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)"

My radicular pain has continued through 9 months of progressive symptoms and has not responded to conservative management that included 8 weeks and 24 visits of supervised physical therapy (2026-05-13 to 2026-07-08), 8 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. That exceeds the six weeks the policy names.

I am not asserting the other alternatives in this list — those addressing cord compression, myelopathy, spondylotic angulation or subluxation measurements, or a synovial cyst — because my records do not contain those findings. Under the plan's own wording, only **any one** of the listed criteria must apply, and my records satisfy the two quoted above. If Anthem applied a criterion from the portion of the list not reproduced in the excerpts available to me, I ask that it be identified in writing.

**7. Pain and functional impairment.** The guideline states:

> "significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs"

My records document 9 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain, numbness into the right thumb and index finger, and weakness. For the specific numbers this definition uses, please refer to [documented pain rating out of 10, from the office note of [date]] and [the specific ADLs/IADLs I am unable to perform, as documented in the office note of [date]]. My surgeon's office can supply these on request if they were not highlighted in the original submission.

**8. Waiver provision.** For completeness, the guideline also states:

> "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when myelopathy, weakness, or bladder disturbance is present."

I raise this only as an additional point: my records document weakness. Regardless, I completed a full course of conservative management, so the prerequisite is satisfied on its own terms.

**9. Surgical risk factor.** The guideline states:

> "Tobacco cessation. Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to spinal surgery is strongly recommended to reduce the risk of pseudoarthrosis."

My records document that I am a non-smoker. They also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

## What the denial notice said

The notice of 2026-08-02 does not identify which specific criterion in the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* was not met; it states only that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. Because the records appear to me to satisfy the criteria quoted above, I am asking that the reconsideration be conducted against the guideline's actual language, and that if the decision is upheld, Anthem specify in writing the exact criterion and the exact record it found lacking.

## Closing request

I respectfully ask that Anthem overturn the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22551 and approve the procedure. I also request:

1. A copy of the specific clinical criteria used in this determination;
2. The name and specialty of the reviewer who made it; and
3. Review by a physician of the same or similar specialty as my treating surgeon.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-01-29** (180 days from the date of the notice), and I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I am also able to submit through anthem.com or the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card, and I will confirm receipt.

**Enclosures:** Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-02 (Reference POC-ACAA2D5BAD-67552); MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-06-07; physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-13 to 2026-07-08, 24 visits); office notes from Dr. Lindqvist; record of corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-18; [any additional records].

Thank you for your time and for reconsidering this decision.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
Riley Ellison
Member ID: W168862914
Date of birth: [DOB]
Reference number: POC-ACAA2D5BAD-67552
[Phone] | [Email]
